description: `from` and `server` as names: a parameter (`isModule(from)`, `bump(server)`), a `let` (`let from = server; from = from + 1`), destructuring (`const { from, server } = e`), a field (`e.server`) and a member receiver (`from.startsWith(…)`). After the click @out is "scrml:data|mod|no" and @n is bump(4) + 4 = 9.
rationale: §54.3: "`from` SHALL NOT be a reserved word outside this position. Existing code that uses `from` as a parameter name, local binding, or field name (e.g., `function foo(from: number) { return from + 1 }`) SHALL continue to compile without change." `server` is a function modifier before `function` / `fn` only (§52.10); no SPEC sentence reserves it, and §7.2 admits the JavaScript name. The bootstrap lexed `.startsWith` after `from` as a bare variant (E-STMT-MISSING-SEMICOLON) and refused `let from` (E-PARSE-LOCAL) and `{ from, server }` (E-STMT-BINDING-NAME).
